message.content:
You are probing a pre-compiled Python executable to reverse-engineer exact behavior.

The executable at /workspace/dataset/test16_executable runs exactly this Python:

    import yaml, argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), Dumper=yaml.SafeDumper)
    print(result)

Invoke it as:  /workspace/dataset/test16_executable --a 'YAML TEXT'
Use single-quoted bash strings, or printf/heredoc into a shell variable, for inputs containing quotes/newlines/backslashes.
To see exact whitespace and newlines, pipe through `cat -A` or `od -c`. ALWAYS capture the exit code (`echo "RC=$?"`).
Batch many probes per bash call (a for-loop over inputs) — you should run MANY DOZENS of distinct inputs.
Note: the trailing print() adds one extra newline beyond yaml.dump's own trailing newline.

Your goal is a precise, implementable behavioral spec for a from-scratch JavaScript reimplementation.
Do NOT write any implementation code. Do NOT read Python library source. Probe empirically, then generalize into rules.
Be exhaustive within your assigned area, including nasty edge cases and error cases (report the error class name and message shape, and the exit code).

YOUR ASSIGNED AREA:
The DUMP side style choice and escaping for STRING values (and how non-strings render).
Determine exactly when a string is emitted plain vs 'single-quoted' vs "double-quoted", and the escaping rules.
Probe strings (pass them in via double-quoted YAML input so you control the exact string, e.g. --a '{k: "VALUE"}' or --a '"VALUE"'):
strings that look like numbers/bools/nulls (123, 1.5, true, no, null, ~, .inf, 0x1f, 1:20, 2001-12-14);
empty string ""; strings of only spaces; leading space; trailing space; internal double spaces; leading/trailing tabs;
strings starting with indicators - ? : , [ ] { } # & * ! | > % @ ` " ' and with "- ", "? ", ": ", " #";
strings containing ": " or " #" in the middle; strings containing only "-"; "---"; "..."; "<<";
strings with newlines (one, several, leading newline, trailing newline, consecutive newlines, ONLY newlines);
strings with control chars (\x00 \x07 \x08 \t \x0b \x0c \r \x1b \x85 \xa0 \u2028 \u2029 \ufeff);
non-ASCII (é, 中文, emoji with surrogate pairs, \u00a0) — check whether they are escaped as \xNN / \uNNNN / \UNNNNNNNN or emitted raw (allow_unicode default);
backslashes and quotes inside strings; a single "'" ; a single '"'.
Report the EXACT emitted bytes for each (use cat -A). Derive the full precedence rule and the double-quote escape table.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.category: dump-side string style selection and escaping (PyYAML SafeDumper emitter)
rules:
OUTPUT FRAME: stdout is yaml.dump(...) (which already ends in exactly one 
) plus one more 
 from print(). So every successful run's stdout ends with "

". Exit code 0.

DOCUMENT-END MARKER: if and only if the ROOT node is a scalar emitted in PLAIN style, an extra line "...
" is appended after the scalar (before print()'s newline). Root scalars emitted single- or double-quoted, root block scalars (!!binary), and root collections (including empty '{}' / '[]') get NO '...' line. Examples: 'hello' -> "hello
...

"; '"123"' -> "'123'

"; 123 -> "123
...

"; [] -> "[]

".

GLOBAL EMITTER SETTINGS (fixed): default_flow_style=False (block style for all non-empty collections; empty dict/list emit as {} / []), indent=2, best_width=80, allow_unicode=False, line_break='\n', explicit_start/end=False, default_style=None. Block scalar styles (| and >) are NEVER chosen automatically; only !!binary uses '!!binary |'.

STYLE PRECEDENCE for a string scalar: (1) PLAIN if allow_block_plain AND the string round-trips as a plain str (i.e. the implicit resolver applied to the plain form yields tag:yaml.org,2002:str) AND not (it is a simple-key context and the string is empty or multiline). (2) else SINGLE-QUOTED if allow_single_quoted AND not (simple-key context and multiline). (3) else DOUBLE-QUOTED.

RESOLVER GUARD (forces quoting of str that would re-read as a non-string). Emit quoted if the string matches any of these (this is the exact PyYAML SafeLoader implicit resolver set): (a) null: '' | '~' | 'null' | 'Null' | 'NULL'; (b) bool: yes|Yes|YES|no|No|NO|true|True|TRUE|false|False|FALSE|on|On|ON|off|Off|OFF (exactly these 18 spellings; 'y','Y','n','N','yEs','oN','nUll' are NOT bools); (c) int: ^[-+]?0b[0-1_]+$ | ^[-+]?0[0-7_]+$ | ^[-+]?(?:0|[1-9][0-9_]*)$ | ^[-+]?0x[0-9a-fA-F_]+$ | ^[-+]?[1-9][0-9_]*(?::[0-5]?[0-9])+$ ; (d) float: ^[-+]?[0-9][0-9_]*\.[0-9_]*(?:[eE][-+][0-9]+)?$ | ^\.[0-9_]+(?:[eE][-+][0-9]+)?$ | ^[-+]?[0-9][0-9_]*(?::[0-5]?[0-9])+\.[0-9_]*$ | ^[-+]?\.(?:inf|Inf|INF)$ | ^\.(?:nan|NaN|NAN)$ ; (e) merge: '<<'; (f) value: '='; (g) timestamp: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$ or the long form ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{1,2}-[0-9]{1,2}([Tt]|[ \t]+)[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]*)?(([ \t]*)Z|[-+][0-9]{1,2}(:[0-9]{2})?)?$ .  NOTE the exponent alternative requires an explicit sign: '1.5e3' and '1e+5' are NOT floats (stay plain) while '1.0e+3','1.5E+3','1.5e-3' are; and '.5' is a float but '-.5'/'+.5' are not.

SCALAR ANALYSIS (compute these flags over the string; used to decide allow_*): leading_space = s[0]==' '; trailing_space = s[-1]==' '; leading_break = s[0] is a break; trailing_break = s[-1] is a break; where 'break' means one of \n, \x85,  ,  .  break_space = some break is immediately followed by ' '.  space_break = some ' ' is immediately followed by a break.  line_breaks = any break present.  special_characters = any char c with NOT (c=='\n' or '\x20'<=c<='\x7E'); note that because allow_unicode is False, EVERY non-ASCII char counts as special, and so do \t and \r and all C0/C1 controls and DEL.

INDICATOR FLAGS: set block_indicators=True (and flow_indicators=True) if s starts with '---' or '...'. For index 0: if s[0] is one of  # , [ ] { } & * ! | > ' " % @ `  -> block_indicators=True. If s[0] is '?' or ':' -> block_indicators=True only when the next char is whitespace/EOS (whitespace set = \0, ' ', \t, \r, \n, \x85,  ,  , or end of string). If s[0]=='-' -> block_indicators=True only when followed by whitespace/EOS. For index>0: ':' -> block_indicators=True only when followed by whitespace/EOS; '#' -> block_indicators=True only when preceded by whitespace (space, tab, or a break). Characters , ? [ ] { } at index>0 only set flow_indicators, which is irrelevant here because output is always block context.

ALLOW FLAGS: start with allow_block_plain=allow_single_quoted=allow_double_quoted=True. If leading_space or leading_break or trailing_space or trailing_break -> allow_block_plain=False. If space_break or special_characters -> allow_block_plain=False and allow_single_quoted=False. If break_space -> allow_block_plain=False and allow_single_quoted=False. If line_breaks -> allow_block_plain=False. If block_indicators -> allow_block_plain=False. Empty string: allow_block_plain=True, allow_single_quoted=True, but the resolver guard makes '' resolve to null so it is emitted as ''.

NET EFFECT SUMMARY: DOUBLE-QUOTED is chosen exactly when the string contains any char outside [\x20-\x7E] other than '\n' (so: tab, CR, NUL, any control, DEL, any char >= \x80 including \xa0/ /﻿/emoji), OR contains ' ' immediately before a break, OR contains a break immediately before ' '. SINGLE-QUOTED is chosen for everything else that cannot be plain (leading/trailing space, any newline, leading indicator char, ': ' or trailing ':', ' #', leading '---'/'...', or resolver collision). Otherwise PLAIN.

PLAIN EMISSION: write the raw string. Line folding: scan the string; whenever a run of spaces of length exactly 1 ends and the current output column is > 80, replace that single space with a line break plus the continuation indent; runs of 2+ spaces are never folded. The continuation indent equals (the column at which the key or '- ' item content starts) + 2 — e.g. 2 for a top-level mapping value or root scalar, 4 for a value one level deeper, etc. Plain scalars never contain a newline by construction.

SINGLE-QUOTED EMISSION: write ' then the content with every ' doubled to '', then '. Break runs: a run of N consecutive break chars is written as N+1 physical line breaks followed by the continuation indent (i.e. one 
 in the value becomes "

<indent>"; two 
 become "


<indent>"). Blank lines produced this way carry NO trailing whitespace. Space folding: when a run of exactly one space ends, and the run does not start at offset 0, and the run does not end at the end of the string, and the current output column is > 80, emit a line break + continuation indent instead of the space. Column counting uses the emitted characters (so doubled '' count as 2).

DOUBLE-QUOTED EMISSION: write " ... ". A character is escaped iff it is '"', '\\', \x85,  ,  , ﻿, or is outside \x20-\x7E. Escape table (checked first): \0 -> \0, \x07 -> \a, \x08 -> \b, \x09 -> \t, \x0A -> \n, \x0B -> \v, \x0C -> \f, \x0D -> \r, \x1B -> \e, '"' -> \", '\\' -> \\, \x85 -> \N, \xA0 -> \_,   -> \L,   -> \P. Otherwise: codepoint <= 0xFF -> \xHH; <= 0xFFFF -> \uHHHH; else -> \UHHHHHHHH. Hex digits are UPPERCASE, zero-padded to 2/4/8. Space, '/', "'" are NOT escaped.

DOUBLE-QUOTED FOLDING: while scanning, at index i (strictly 0 < i < len-1), if the current char is a space OR we have just flushed/emitted an escape at this position, and (current column + length of the pending unflushed plain chunk) > 80, then emit the pending chunk followed by a '\\' character, then a line break + continuation indent; if the next character to be emitted is a space, emit an extra '\\' immediately after the indent (so the line resumes with "\\ "). A long run of ordinary printable non-space characters is never folded (there is no flush point).

NON-STRING RENDERING (all plain, unquoted): int -> Python decimal repr (0x1F->31, 0b101->5, 007->7, 1:20->80, -0->0, 685_230->685230). float -> Python repr with these overrides: infinity -> .inf / -.inf, NaN -> .nan; otherwise repr(f) e.g. 0.5, 5.0, 1000.0. bool -> true / false. None -> null. datetime.date -> ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'; datetime.datetime -> str(dt) i.e. 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.ffffff][+HH:MM]' (space separator, microseconds zero-padded to 6, offset as +HH:MM). bytes -> '!!binary |' followed by base64 on indented lines. A set loaded via !!set -> '!!set' tag then mapping entries with null values.

MAPPING KEYS: a key is written inline ("key: value") only if it is a simple key: not empty, not multiline, and len(key_string) + 5 < 128 (the +5 is the length of the implicit tag shorthand '!!str'/'!!int'/etc.), i.e. plain string keys up to 122 chars are inline and 123+ chars become explicit. Non-simple keys are written as '? <key>' on its own line, then ': <value>' on the next line. In simple-key context an empty or multiline scalar is disallowed as plain, and a multiline scalar is disallowed as single-quoted — but since such keys become explicit keys, the simple-key restriction no longer applies and they end up single-quoted.

ERROR CASE (load side, before any dumping): characters not allowed by the YAML reader (e.g. U+FFFE, U+FFFF, other non-printables introduced literally) raise yaml.reader.ReaderError with message 'unacceptable character #x<hex>: special characters are not allowed\n  in "<unicode string>", position N'. A Python traceback is printed to stderr followed by '[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test16' due to unhandled exception!', stdout is empty, exit code 1.
surprises:
Root-level PLAIN scalars get an extra '...' document-end line, but root-level quoted scalars and collections do not. So `--a hello` prints "hello
...

" while `--a '"hello"'` prints "hello
...

" only if it re-resolves plain — but `--a '"123"'` prints "'123'

" with no '...'.

A string containing a newline is NOT emitted as a block literal (|) or folded (>) scalar. It is emitted as a MULTI-LINE SINGLE-QUOTED scalar in which each newline becomes a blank line: "a\nb" -> k: 'a<NL><NL>  b'. Two newlines become three physical newlines.
TAB is treated as a 'special character', not whitespace: any string containing \t is forced to double-quoted style, even 'a\tb'.

allow_unicode is False, so ALL non-ASCII is escaped: é -> \xE9, 中 -> 中, emoji -> \U0001F600 (one 8-digit escape for the astral codepoint, not surrogate pairs). Hex digits are uppercase but the 'x'/'u'/'U' prefix letters keep their case.
\x85 (NEL) and \xA0 (NBSP) get the rare named escapes \N and \_;  /  get \L/\P; ﻿ gets ﻿ (it is explicitly excluded from the 'printable unicode' set even when allow_unicode is on).
Internal runs of multiple spaces do NOT force quoting ('a  b' stays plain), but a single leading or trailing space does.

The exact placement of a space relative to a newline flips single- vs double-quoting: 'a
b' -> single-quoted multiline, but 'a 
b' and 'a
 b' -> double-quoted with literal 
 escapes.

'-x', '?x', ':x' are plain (indicator only matters when followed by whitespace/EOS), but ',x', '[x', '#x', '&x', '!x', '%x', '@x', '`x', '|x', '>x' are quoted even though , [ # etc. are only flow indicators — PyYAML sets block_indicators for them at position 0 too.
'0o17' stays a plain STRING (PyYAML's int resolver has no 0o form), whereas '0x1f', '0b101' and '007' are quoted. Likewise '0X1F' and '0B1' are plain (case-sensitive prefixes).

'1e5' and '1e+5' are plain strings, but '1.0e+3' is quoted: PyYAML's float regex requires a decimal point, and requires an explicit sign on the exponent. Also '.5' is a float but '-.5' and '+.5' are not.
'y', 'Y', 'n', 'N' are NOT booleans and stay plain, while 'yes'/'Yes'/'YES'/'on'/'On'/'ON'/'off' etc. are quoted. Case must be all-lower, Title, or all-UPPER — 'yEs' and 'oN' are plain.
Any string starting with '---' or '...' is quoted, so '----' is quoted while '--' and '..' are plain.
'<<' and '=' alone are quoted (merge-key and value resolvers), but '<<x' and '=x' are plain.

Double-quoted line folding uses a trailing backslash continuation, and when the fold lands on a space the next line begins with a backslash-space: ...wo\\<NL>  \\ wo... . Single-quoted/plain folding just replaces a single space with a newline+indent; runs of 2+ spaces are never folded.
Line width folding only replaces runs of EXACTLY one space; a string of 'wo   wo   ...' (3-space runs) is emitted on one 100+ column line with no folding at all.
Mapping keys go explicit ('? key' / ': value') at 123 characters, not 128, because the emitter's simple-key length budget includes the 5-character implicit tag shorthand ('!!str').
